# Answer: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **mirror the cyan template horizontally
around the green anchor before stamping it at the red markers**. It fits every
canonical demonstration because every canonical cyan template is horizontally
symmetric.

An exact disagreement is the production case in
`repo/generators/8de1c257a9c7/counterexamples/horizontal_mirror_seed29_slot1.json`:
seed `29`, sample index `1`, difficulty `medium`. The 17×16 input has an
asymmetric hook anchored by the green cell at `(11,3)`, cyan cells at
`(9,3),(10,3),(10,4),(11,4),(12,4),(12,5)`, and red markers at
`(9,2),(10,2),(11,2)`. Exact offset transplantation and horizontal mirroring
disagree in 16 output cells.

I checked it three ways:

1. the retained JSON records the full input, intended output, rival output, and
   `differing_cells: 16`;
2. the frozen regression calls the production generator at `(29,1,"medium")`,
   checks that the retained input is reproduced, and compares both executable
   Python rules;
3. the selected canonical Racket execution retained at
   `repo/generators/8de1c257a9c7/counterexamples/current-shortcut/checks/mirror-counterexample/racket-final-v311.json`
   matches the intended output.

Yes, the production generator emits such cases: the eight-slot schedule contains
asymmetric hook and stair profiles. The final 300-lesson census reports the
horizontal-mirror rival refuted in all 100 lessons of each difficulty band, with
0/1,500 production ambiguities and 0/1,500 held-out-query ambiguities against the
declared rivals. The proposed parametric prototype also materializes this rival
as a real alternative setting; its teaching episodes use asymmetric inputs so
the setting is inferable rather than silently ambiguous.
